sentences.text: The eyeballs of Malawania were supported by scleral rings made of 13 bones.
The neural spines at the front of Malawania have unique trapezoidal tops.
Malawania has unusually short, trapezoid-shaped humeri, a feature unique to this genus.
The upper end of each humerus in Malawania bears a unique backwards-pointing capitular process.
The lower ends of the humeri in Malawania do not broaden significantly and articulate with the radius and ulna.
Malawania had four digits in its foreflippers, with two originating from each intermedium bone.
The first digit of Malawania would have had more than nine phalanges when complete, with the first bearing a notch.
Malawania is nicknamed the "out-of-time swimmer" because its primitive anatomy contrasts sharply with its Early Cretaceous age.

Malawania is recognized as the first non-ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur known to have survived past the Jurassic–Cretaceous boundary, approximately 66 million years after the group was previously thought to have gone extinct.
The only known specimen of Malawania was discovered in 1952 in Iraqi Kurdistan by a team of British petroleum geologists led by Douglas M. Morton.
The specimen was donated to the Natural History Museum, London, in 1959 and catalogued as NHMUK PV R6682.
The specimen was formally described as the new species Malawania anachronus in 2013 by Valentin Fischer and colleagues.
Malawania belongs to the kingdom Animalia.
Malawania is a member of the phylum Chordata.
Malawania is placed within the class Sauropsida.
Malawania is classified in the order Ichthyosauria.
Malawania belongs to the suborder Thunnosauria.
Malawania is classified within the family Ichthyosauridae.
The type species of the genus Malawania is Malawania anachronus.
The genus Malawania was named by Fischer and colleagues in 2013.
Fischer and colleagues classified Malawania anachronus as a basal member of Thunnosauria in their 2013 study.
In 2025, Lomax and colleagues recovered Malawania within the Ichthyosauridae as part of a clade containing all recognized members of the family.
Malawania was an extinct basal thunnosaurian ichthyosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous in what is now Iraq.
Malawania lived between 132.6 and 121.4 million years ago during the Hauterivian to Barremian stages.
A 2017 study by Lomax and colleagues recovered Malawania as a basal thunnosaur with Ichthyosaurus as the sister taxon of Protoichthyosaurus.
